### 2. How to Verify a Lawyer’s Standing

Before hiring any attorney, you should perform two quick checks:

1.  **Check the California State Bar:** Visit [calbar.ca.gov](https://www.calbar.ca.gov/) to ensure the attorney is active, licensed to practice in California, and has no history of public discipline.
2.  **Alameda County Bar Association Referral Service:** You can contact the **ACBA** (acbanet.org) or the **East Bay Community Law Center** for local lawyer referrals who are vetted and in good standing.

---

### 3. Key Questions to Ask During Your Free Consultation

Almost all reputable personal injury attorneys offer **free consultations** and work on a **contingency fee basis** (meaning you pay no upfront costs, and they only get paid if you win or settle your case—usually 33% to 40% of the settlement).

When you call, ask these questions to find the best fit:

*   **Experience:** *"How many cases like mine (e.g., truck accident, slip and fall) have you handled in the last two years?"*
*   **Results:** *"What is your typical settlement or verdict range for injuries of my severity?"*
*   **Management:** *"Will you personally handle my case, or will it be handed off to a junior associate or paralegal?"*
*   **Trial Readiness:** *"Are you willing to take this case to trial if the insurance company offers an unfair settlement?"*

---

### Recommended Next Steps
If you or a loved one were injured recently, schedule 2 to 3 free consultations with different local attorneys to compare their approach, communication style, and fee structures before signing an agreement.
